cases.who: TIME (Callum Sutherland and Olivia-Anne Cleary); ABC News Australia (Rudi Maxwell with wires; headline and summary)
cases.date: Sep 24, 2026 (TIME article; ABC News Australia headline and summary)
cases.label: TIME (Callum Sutherland and Olivia-Anne Cleary); ABC News Australia (Rudi Maxwell with wires; headline and summary) · Sep 24, 2026 (TIME article; ABC News Australia headline and summary)
cases.said: TIME and ABC News (Australia) reported that a federal judge “ordered President Donald Trump” to restore CNN, MS NOW and Politico’s White House press access.
cases.record: The order expressly leaves the President out. The substance (the administration was ordered to restore the passes) is accurate; the error is naming Trump as the person ordered. One case per claim: TIME and ABC News Australia repeat the same error, so they share this row. ABC Australia's story is marked Reuters/ABC; Reuters' own wording was not verified, so Reuters is not named. No correction or fact-check found as of Sep 24, 2026. Claim as published: https://time.com/article/2026/09/24/judge-overturns-trump-white-house-media-ban-temporary-order-appeal/ ; https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-24/us-judge-reverses-donald-trump-media-ban-cnn-politico-ms-now/107192236 Also: https://abcnews.com/US/judge-orders-white-house-restore-press-passes-cnn/story?id=136709442 ; https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/74823502/cable-news-network-inc-v-trump/ Primary record: TRO, CNN v. Trump, No. 1:26-cv-03287-TJK (D.D.C. Sep 24, 2026), ECF 24 ¶2: “Defendants (except for President Trump) and their agents, representatives, and all persons or entities acting in concert with them shall immediately return, reinstate, and restore the White House ‘hard pass’ press credentials…”

cases.label: NPR (David Folkenflik; syndicated by GPB) · Sep 23, 2026 (NPR, syndicated by GPB)
cases.said: NPR said Trump “barred the Associated Press from the White House” in 2025 over the Gulf of America dispute, presenting it as a precedent for the 2026 ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
cases.record: In 2025 the AP was kept out of the press pool, the Oval Office, Air Force One and many East Room events, but it kept its hard passes and general access to the White House press facilities. The 2026 action revoked hard passes and blocked the whole complex, so the comparison makes the 2025 restriction look like the 2026 ban. Rated misleading, not false, because “barred” is accurate for specific events. No correction or fact-check found as of Sep 24, 2026. Claim as published: https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/09/23/major-news-outlets-banned-by-trump-will-have-their-day-in-court Primary record: AP v. Budowich, No. 1:25-cv-00532-TNM (D.D.C. Apr. 8, 2025), ECF 46 at 9: “The parties agree that no AP employee's hard pass has been revoked”; at 12: “both parties agreed that the AP's hard pass status had been unchanged.”

cases.record: Debt rose ~$7.8T under Trump; CBO Jan 2017 already projected large rises; TCJA needed Congress; COVID spending major. FactCheck: Trump alone not responsible for all debt added. Also: https://www.cbo.gov/publication/52370; https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/debt-to-the-penny/debt-to-the-penny

cases.date: Jul 2021 (Jeffries remarks; WaPo Fact Checker column Jul 20, 2021)
cases.label: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries · Jul 2021 (Jeffries remarks; WaPo Fact Checker column Jul 20, 2021)
cases.said: Reconciliation was used in 2017 to pass the GOP tax scam where '83 percent of the benefits went to the wealthiest 1 percent' (Jeffries zombie claim).
cases.record: WaPo Kessler: 83% is 2027 figure after sunsets; 2018 top 1% share 20.5%. Same incomplete talking point PolitiFact rated Half True for Pelosi/DNC. Distinct speaker from Pelosi 2021 case. Also: https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2021/mar/16/nancy-pelosi/nancy-pelosi-repeats-incomplete-talking-point-2017/; https://taxpolicycenter.org/sites/default/files/publication/150816/2001641_distributional_analysis_of_the_conference_agreement_for_the_tax_cuts_and_jobs_act_0.pdf

cases.said: Donald Trump 'issued a Muslim ban as president' (implying a ban on all Muslims).
cases.record: FactCheck: 2017 EOs/proclamation restricted nationals of listed countries (not all Muslims); Pew: first EO would have affected ~12% of world Muslims. Primary = EO text. cases.label: Rep. Lisa Blunt Rochester · Aug 21, 2024 (Lisa Blunt Rochester DNC night 3)
cases.said: Trump 'wrote' Project 2025.
cases.record: FactCheck: Trump did not write Project 2025; Heritage Mandate for Leadership; Trump said it doesn't speak for him. Proven false authorship claim. Primary points to Heritage Project 2025 authorship/home (not Trump). Also: https://www.project2025.org/

cases.label: Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg · Aug 21, 2024 (Buttigieg DNC night 3)
cases.said: The only economic promise Trump kept was to 'cut taxes for the rich' (implying no broader tax cuts).
cases.record: FactCheck cites TPC: TCJA would reduce taxes on average for all income groups in 2018 and 2025. Distinct from Fox 'billionaire-only' batch5 item—this is Buttigieg DNC line. 'cut taxes for the rich' phrase HIT in corpus may be different claim—verify. Also: https://taxpolicycenter.org/sites/default/files/publication/150816/2001641_distributional_analysis_of_the_conference_agreement_for_the_tax_cuts_and_jobs_act_0.pdf

cases.record: Attkisson #91. Primary = White House released call memorandum. Also: https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/

cases.label: Donald Trump (2016 campaign), Twitter post · Nov 22, 2015
cases.said: Posted a crime graphic claiming “Whites killed by blacks — 81%” and “Whites killed by whites — 16%.”
cases.record: Primary record: FBI Expanded Homicide Data Table 6 (2014), white victims: 3,021 total; 2,488 white offenders (82.4%); 446 Black offenders (14.8%). The graphic's 81% and 16% are wrong.

cases.who: Donald Trump (2016 campaign), rally in Concord, N.C.
cases.label: Donald Trump (2016 campaign), rally in Concord, N.C. · Mar 7, 2016
cases.said: Said the U.S. has a “$500 billion a year trade deficit with China.”
cases.record: Primary record: Census: “The deficit with China increased $22.6 billion to $365.7 billion in 2015.” BEA gives the same $365.7 billion.

cases.label: Hillary Clinton (D), news conference · Mar 10, 2015
cases.said: Said: “I did not email any classified material to anyone on my email. There is no classified material.”
cases.record: Primary record: FBI Director Comey, July 5, 2016: 110 emails in 52 email chains contained classified information at the time they were sent or received.

cases.who: Hillary Clinton (D), Fox News Sunday interview
cases.label: Hillary Clinton (D), Fox News Sunday interview · Jul 31, 2016
cases.said: Said: “Director Comey said my answers were truthful.”
cases.record: Primary record: Comey said only that there was no basis to conclude she lied to the FBI; asked about her public statements he said “There was classified material emailed.”

cases.who: Sean Spicer, White House press secretary (R)
cases.label: Sean Spicer, White House press secretary (R) · Jan 21, 2017
cases.said: Said the inauguration drew “the largest audience to ever witness an inauguration — period — both in person and around the globe.”
cases.record: Primary record: WMATA Metro ridership: 570,557 full-day trips in 2017 vs 782,000 (2013) and 1.1 million (2009). The in-person claim is contradicted; no official global audience count exists.

cases.who: Viral social media post (shared by Donald Trump on Twitter)
cases.label: Viral social media post (shared by Donald Trump on Twitter) · Aug 30, 2020
cases.said: Claimed the CDC “quietly updated the Covid number to admit that only 6% of all the 153,504 deaths recorded actually died from Covid.”
cases.record: Primary record: CDC: over 5% of COVID-19 death certificates listed COVID-19 as the only cause; the rest averaged 4.0 additional conditions. The 6% never meant only 6% died from COVID-19.

cases.label: Joe Biden (D), White House remarks · Jan 26, 2023
cases.said: Said: “we cut the deficit by $1.7 trillion, the largest reduction in debt in American history.”
cases.record: Primary record: Treasury: the FY2022 deficit fell $1.4 trillion, but borrowing from the public rose $2.0 trillion to $24.3 trillion. The debt was not reduced.

cases.label: Joe Biden (D), midterm campaign remarks · Nov 2022
cases.said: Said: “for the first time in 10 years, seniors are getting an increase in their Social Security checks” and “We cut the federal debt in half.”
cases.record: Primary record: SSA cost-of-living increases were paid in 2012–2014 and 2016–2021. Treasury: borrowing from the public rose $2.0 trillion in FY2022; debt was not cut in half.

cases.label: Joe Biden (D), interview remarks · May 2024
cases.said: Said: “It was 9% when I came to office, 9%.”
cases.record: Primary record: BLS: 12-month CPI inflation was 1.4% in January 2021; it peaked at 9.1% in June 2022, under Biden.

cases.who: Joe Biden (D), U.S. Conference of Mayors remarks
cases.label: Joe Biden (D), U.S. Conference of Mayors remarks · Jan 2023
cases.said: Said: “Two years ago this week, 18 million people were out of work ... Now that number is under 1.6 million.”
cases.record: Primary record: BLS: about 10.2 million unemployed in January 2021 and 5.7 million in December 2022. The 18 million and 1.6 million figures were unemployment-benefit recipients, not the unemployed.

cases.label: Kash Patel, FBI Director (R administration) · 2025
cases.said: Took credit for the drop in violent crime, including the 2024 decline that came before he took office.
cases.record: Primary record: FBI: violent crime fell 4.5% in 2024, before Patel became director, and 9.3% in 2025. The FBI's own page credits agencies working together.
